Combined 3D motion

plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates how the 3D motion of a point projects into 2D motion on the image plane under a pinhole camera model. A 3D point P moves through space with instantaneous velocity Ṗ, and the green line from the camera center O through P shows the projection ray, which pierces the image plane at the corresponding 2D image point p. The red arrow at P labeled Ṗ marks the point's 3D velocity, while the red arrow at p labeled ṗ marks the resulting instantaneous velocity of its 2D projection; the dashed line traces where the displaced 3D point projects, making clear that the 2D velocity is the projection of the 3D velocity rather than a simple rescaling of it. This figure motivates the perspective-projection relations x = fX/Z and y = fY/Z, and their time derivatives, as the mathematical link between a point's 3D velocity Ṗ = (Ẋ, Ẏ, Ż) in world coordinates and its observed 2D optical flow ṗ = (ẋ, ẏ) in the camera plane.

elements: camera center O as a large black point at the lower-left
label O beside the camera center
rectangular image plane between O and P, drawn as a tall dark-outlined parallelogram with white or transparent interior
solid bright green projection ray from O through the image-plane point p to the 3D point P
2D image point p as a small black point lying on the image plane
label p beside the image point
3D point P as a large black point in space to the right of the image plane
label P beside the 3D point
red velocity arrow at P labeled Ṗ, starting at P and pointing up-left toward the displaced 3D point
red image velocity arrow at p labeled ṗ, starting at p and pointing up-left along the image plane toward the displaced projected point
dashed bright green projection ray from O through the displaced image point p' to the displaced 3D point P'
faint or translucent green segment where the projection ray passes through the image plane
arrowheads on both red velocity vectors
large serif math labels O, p, ṗ, P, and Ṗ

interactions.teaches: The learner sees that P moves in 3D space while p is constrained to the flat image plane, making the projection geometry spatial rather than merely a 2D drawing
Dragging P along its straight 3D trajectory shows that the image point p follows the perspective projection of that motion, not a simple copied displacement

interactions.label: Ẋ
interactions.teaches: A lateral X component changes the horizontal image velocity through the term fẊ/Z, with the same 3D speed producing less image motion at larger depth

interactions.label: Ẏ
interactions.teaches: A vertical Y component changes the vertical image velocity through the term fẎ/Z, again scaled by the point's depth

interactions.label: Ż
interactions.teaches: Motion toward or away from the camera creates radial optical flow because the image coordinates contain the changing denominator Z

demo_steps.title: Combined 3D motion
demo_steps.narration: The point P moves up-left in 3D, and the dashed green ray shows where its displaced position projects. The shorter red arrow on the image plane is the resulting optical flow ṗ.

demo_steps.title: Pure horizontal motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ẋ nonzero, the projected point mostly slides horizontally on the image plane. Its speed is reduced by depth through ẋ = fẊ/Z.

demo_steps.title: Pure vertical motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ẏ nonzero, the optical flow points vertically on the image plane. The 3D displacement is filtered through the same perspective scale factor f/Z.

demo_steps.title: Pure depth motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ż nonzero, P moves along the viewing direction, but p still moves unless it is exactly on the optical axis. This is the radial flow caused by the changing perspective denominator.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a pinhole camera coordinate system with O at (0, 0, 0), optical axis along +Z, image plane at Z=f with f=2.0. The image plane is a vertical rectangle of width 3.2 world units in camera X and height 4.4 world units in camera Y, centered near (0, 0, 2); draw only a thick dark outline, color #2b2f33, line width visually heavy. Default 3D point P = (1.25, 0.35, 7.5), so its projection is p = (fX/Z, fY/Z, f) ≈ (0.33, 0.09, 2). Solid projection ray runs from O through p to P and is bright green #19e000, thick. Default velocity is Ṗ = (Ẋ, Ẏ, Ż) = (-0.8, 0.6, -0.9); draw the red arrow from P to P + sṖ with s≈0.8 so it points screen up-left as in the source. Displaced point P' = P + dtṖ with dt≈0.8; p' = (fX'/Z', fY'/Z', f). Draw dashed green ray O-p'-P' using the same green, dash length about 0.18 units. Image velocity vector is ṗ = (ẋ, ẏ) where ẋ = f(ẊZ - XŻ)/Z² and ẏ = f(ẎZ - YŻ)/Z²; draw the red image-plane arrow from p toward p + dt(ẋ, ẏ, 0) on the image plane, scaled so it is visible but smaller than the 3D arrow. Points are black #020202 with subtle dark gray outer rims; O and P radius about 0.13 units, p radius about 0.08 units. Labels are large black serif text matching the source: O at lower-left of the camera point, p below/right of image point, ṗ above the small red arrow, P to the right of the large 3D point, Ṗ above the large red arrow.
interactionPlan.notes: Keep the initial camera view close to the source: image plane on the left, O slightly lower-left of the plane, P far to the right, solid ray rising gently across the frame, and velocity arrows pointing up-left. Recompute p, p', both green rays, and both red arrows whenever P is dragged or any velocity slider changes. Constrain dragging of P to remain in front of the camera with Z > f + 0.5; implement drag along the current straight trajectory direction defined by Ṗ, with a fallback free 3D drag handle if Ṗ is zero. Use CSS2D or SDF text for labels so they remain readable during orbit. Use LineDashedMaterial for the displaced projection ray and cone+cylinder arrow geometry for red vectors.

authoredContext:
A 3D point will follow a trajectory $\mathbf{P}(t) = (X(t),Y(t),Z(t))$,
in camera coordinates (-optical_flow_basic_motion_point). As the
point moves, it has an instantaneous 3D velocity of
$\dot{\mathbf{P}} = (\dot{X}(t), \dot{Y}(t), \dot{Z}(t))$. The
projection of this point into the image plane location is
$\mathbf{p}(t) = (x(t),y(t))$ and its projection will move with the 2D
instantaneous velocity $\dot{\mathbf{p}} = (\dot{x}(t), \dot{y}(t))$,
where all the derivatives are done with respect to time, $t$.

A 3D point, $\mathbf{P}$, moving in the world projects a 2D moving point, $\mathbf{p}$, into the camera plane.

discrepancies: The image plane is much smaller and more centered than in the source, where it dominates the left half of the figure and the ray passes through it at a shallow angle.
The 3D red velocity arrow for P is barely visible and does not match the large left-up red arrow shown at the right in the source.
The projected red velocity arrow at p is too small and visually collapses into the p point rather than appearing as a distinct arrow on the image plane.
The black P point and its displaced/dotted position are not clearly separated; the P and P-dot labels crowd together compared with the well-separated labels in the source.
The dashed green ray is present but does not reproduce the source composition where it runs clearly above the solid ray from the image-plane region toward the displaced point.
evaluation.notes: The main perspective-projection relationship is represented with useful controls, but the proportions, arrow prominence, and label separation differ noticeably from the source.
action_items: Enlarge and reposition the image plane so it occupies the left side like the source figure.
Increase the length and visibility of both red velocity arrows, especially the 3D arrow at P.
Separate the P and P-dot markers and labels so the displacement is visually clear.
Adjust the default viewpoint/composition so the solid and dashed green rays match the source's shallow, horizontally extended layout.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactions are solid, but the critic identifies implementation-level scale, arrow visibility, label separation, and camera composition issues that the generator can fix.

The projected image point p is not clearly shown as a black dot with rim because it is visually dominated by the red arrow/marker at the plane.
The source composition has a much larger left image plane occupying the figure; the generated plane is too small/narrow relative to the rays and points.
evaluation.notes: The main projection-flow elements and labels are present and conceptually correct, but the default camera/view makes the image plane nearly edge-on and the ray separation much less like the source.
action_items: Change the initial camera/root orientation so the image plane appears as a large oblique rectangle with its face visible, matching the source.
Increase the default displacement/velocity direction so the dashed green ray separates clearly upward from the solid green ray as in the reference.
Resize and reposition the image plane to dominate the left side of the composition more strongly.
Make the projected point p visibly black with a rim, not visually swallowed by the red optical-flow arrow.

interactions.teaches: A lateral X component changes the horizontal image velocity through the term fẊ/Z, with the same 3D speed producing less image motion at larger depth

interactions.label: Ẏ
interactions.teaches: A vertical Y component changes the vertical image velocity through the term fẎ/Z, again scaled by the point's depth

interactions.label: Ż
interactions.teaches: Motion toward or away from the camera creates radial optical flow because the image coordinates contain the changing denominator Z

demo_steps.title: Combined 3D motion
demo_steps.narration: The point P moves up-left in 3D, and the dashed green ray shows where its displaced position projects. The shorter red arrow on the image plane is the resulting optical flow ṗ.

demo_steps.title: Pure horizontal motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ẋ nonzero, the projected point mostly slides horizontally on the image plane. Its speed is reduced by depth through ẋ = fẊ/Z.

demo_steps.title: Pure vertical motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ẏ nonzero, the optical flow points vertically on the image plane. The 3D displacement is filtered through the same perspective scale factor f/Z.

demo_steps.title: Pure depth motion
demo_steps.narration: With only Ż nonzero, P moves along the viewing direction, but p still moves unless it is exactly on the optical axis. This is the radial flow caused by the changing perspective denominator.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a pinhole camera coordinate system with O at (0, 0, 0), optical axis along +Z, image plane at Z=f with f=2.0. The image plane is a vertical rectangle of width 3.2 world units in camera X and height 4.4 world units in camera Y, centered near (0, 0, 2); draw only a thick dark outline, color #2b2f33, line width visually heavy. Default 3D point P = (1.25, 0.35, 7.5), so its projection is p = (fX/Z, fY/Z, f) ≈ (0.33, 0.09, 2). Solid projection ray runs from O through p to P and is bright green #19e000, thick. Default velocity is Ṗ = (Ẋ, Ẏ, Ż) = (-0.8, 0.6, -0.9); draw the red arrow from P to P + sṖ with s≈0.8 so it points screen up-left as in the source. Displaced point P' = P + dtṖ with dt≈0.8; p' = (fX'/Z', fY'/Z', f). Draw dashed green ray O-p'-P' using the same green, dash length about 0.18 units. Image velocity vector is ṗ = (ẋ, ẏ) where ẋ = f(ẊZ - XŻ)/Z² and ẏ = f(ẎZ - YŻ)/Z²; draw the red image-plane arrow from p toward p + dt(ẋ, ẏ, 0) on the image plane, scaled so it is visible but smaller than the 3D arrow. Points are black #020202 with subtle dark gray outer rims; O and P radius about 0.13 units, p radius about 0.08 units. Labels are large black serif text matching the source: O at lower-left of the camera point, p below/right of image point, ṗ above the small red arrow, P to the right of the large 3D point, Ṗ above the large red arrow.
interactionPlan.notes: Keep the initial camera view close to the source: image plane on the left, O slightly lower-left of the plane, P far to the right, solid ray rising gently across the frame, and velocity arrows pointing up-left. Recompute p, p', both green rays, and both red arrows whenever P is dragged or any velocity slider changes. Constrain dragging of P to remain in front of the camera with Z > f + 0.5; implement drag along the current straight trajectory direction defined by Ṗ, with a fallback free 3D drag handle if Ṗ is zero. Use CSS2D or SDF text for labels so they remain readable during orbit. Use LineDashedMaterial for the displaced projection ray and cone+cylinder arrow geometry for red vectors.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates how the 3D motion of a point projects into 2D motion on the image plane under a pinhole camera model. A 3D point P moves through space with instantaneous velocity Ṗ, and the green line from the camera center O through P shows the projection ray, which pierces the image plane at the corresponding 2D image point p. The red arrow at P labeled Ṗ marks the point's 3D velocity, while the red arrow at p labeled ṗ marks the resulting instantaneous velocity of its 2D projection; the dashed line traces where the displaced 3D point projects, making clear that the 2D velocity is the projection of the 3D velocity rather than a simple rescaling of it. This figure motivates the perspective-projection relations x = fX/Z and y = fY/Z, and their time derivatives, as the mathematical link between a point's 3D velocity Ṗ = (Ẋ, Ẏ, Ż) in world coordinates and its observed 2D optical flow ṗ = (ẋ, ẏ) in the camera plane.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the 3D point P along its trajectory and watch the 2D projection p move on the image plane
- Sliders for velocity components (X-dot, Y-dot, Z-dot) to show how each affects the 2D optical flow vector

discrepancies: The image plane is drawn as a small nearly front-facing rectangle, while the source shows a much larger oblique plane with strong slanted top and bottom edges dominating the left side.
The camera center O is positioned too close to or overlapping the image plane instead of clearly outside the lower-left of the plane as in the source.

The solid green ray, projected point p, 3D point P, and dashed displaced ray are compressed together; the source has a much longer ray extending far to the right with P well separated from the image plane.
The projected red arrow on the image plane is too small and tucked into the ray, making the p-to-p-dot displacement less visually prominent than in the source.
The labels are mostly correct but their placement differs noticeably: O overlaps the plane edge and P/P-dot are not placed as distinctly relative to their points as in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure captures the projection and optical-flow concept with correct rays, points, arrows, and useful controls, but the viewpoint, plane scale, and spatial layout differ substantially from the source.

Reposition labels to match the source more closely, especially O, p, P, and P-dot.
